requirement:
Model tool descriptions SHOULD NOT explain cases the model meets only
occasionally, such as access policy, excluded or build-output paths, redaction,
paging, and failures, and the harness SHOULD explain each of these where it
occurs: in the tool error, or in a note in the result it affects. The model reads
every description on every assessment, so explaining rare cases there costs
attention on every review for a case most never meet, and access-policy wording
in particular can steer its reasoning away from the review. A tool whose purpose
is one of these cases, such as `next_page`, explains it in its description.
rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

The two SHOULD clauses in `requirements.authoring.tool_descriptions.special_cases` require (1) keeping occasional-case explanations out of general tool descriptions and (2) explaining those cases where they occur. Split by the named cases, these cover access policy, excluded paths, build-output paths, redaction, paging, and failures. A tool dedicated to such a case may explain it in its description.

- **Descriptions:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]` omits these explanations from general tools and describes paging in `next_page`, as permitted. Its reachable `src/github.rs#fn[tool_definition]` also avoids special-case explanations. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[descriptions_leave_paging_policy_redaction_and_failures_to_results]` checks descriptions for special-case wording.
- **Access policy:** `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[PathPolicy]/fn[check_disallow]` explains explicit disallow rules in errors. `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` explains outside-project and untracked-path denials. Coverage includes `src/authoring/access.rs#mod[tests]/fn[evidence_rules_are_literal_paths_not_globs]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[untracked_diagnostics_name_git_add_and_an_allow_rule]`, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors]`, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_read_through_a_symlink_leaving_the_project_returns_an_error_to_the_model]`.
- **Excluded paths:** `SourceAccess::path` explains generated-evidence exclusion. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery]` asserts these diagnostics across read, discovery, and search requests.
- **Build-output paths:** `SourceAccess::path` explains that these paths hold output and directs the model to source. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requests_for_book_or_target_output_are_ordinary_read_failures]` verifies the explanation for book and target output.
- **Redaction:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_redaction_note]`, through `needs_redaction_note`, attaches the explanation in `src/authoring/tools.rs#const[REDACTION_NOTE]` to affected results. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_results_with_redacted_text_carry_the_redaction_note]` checks affected reads and searches and unaffected/literal-marker results.
- **Paging:** `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]` attaches `src/authoring/pages.rs#const[PAGE_NOTE]` when more entries remain. `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order]` reaches `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[all_pages]`, which asserts the explanatory note on intermediate pages and its absence on the last page.
- **Failures:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` sends failed tool dispatches back as tool errors containing their diagnostic. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[malformed_and_failed_reads_return_to_the_model_and_the_assessment_continues]` verifies this for malformed and failed reads.

## Gaps

The general failure explanation is implemented in `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`, but that item has no `{impl}` reference to the subject. It is a caller of the marked tool implementations, not reachable from them by following their calls or types. It therefore needs its own `{impl}` reference to `requirements.authoring.tool_descriptions.special_cases`.

Likewise, `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[malformed_and_failed_reads_return_to_the_model_and_the_assessment_continues]` tests the named failure case but carries only a reference to `requirements.authoring.read_denial`. It needs a `{test}` reference to the subject. The subject-marked denial tests do not replace coverage of ordinary malformed/failed requests.

Neither gap is acknowledged by a supplied or inspected `{fixme}` reference.
